Our Škoda Kodiaq, which is less than three years old, locked itself with the only key inside. Worse still, our dog was trapped in the vehicle.

We have an active Škoda Assistance policy. This was exactly the type of urgent incident for which a manufacturer-backed assistance service should exist. Yet instead of taking responsibility and promptly arranging assistance, we were directed towards our own motor insurer.

That response is disgraceful. The vehicle suffered an apparent locking-system failure, but Škoda’s proposed solution was to pass the cost and responsibility to the customer’s insurance company. Why should an insurer fund recovery arising from a failure involving a nearly new Škoda, especially when the owner already has active Škoda Assistance cover?

A dog was locked inside the car. This was not an inconvenience or a routine enquiry. It was a time-sensitive safety incident. We needed decisive assistance, not an attempt to redirect the problem elsewhere.

The true value of an assistance policy is revealed when something actually goes wrong. On this occasion, Škoda Assistance failed the most basic test: helping its customer during an urgent incident involving one of its own vehicles.

I would strongly advise prospective buyers to ask exactly what Škoda Assistance covers, who pays when the vehicle itself locks the key inside, and whether Škoda will actually send help when it is urgently needed. Our experience has seriously damaged our confidence in both the vehicle and the brand.

I was then offered only half the value of my original glasses towards a replacement, rather than the arrangement initially agreed. As I needed the glasses, I reluctantly paid additional money to purchase a new pair.

I strongly dispute the allegation that I brought broken glasses into the store. I am extremely disappointed by the inconsistent warranty decision, the way I was treated and the additional expense I incurred.

We visited this place on Saturday, 12 September, and actually travelled from Cork specifically to come here. Unfortunately, our experience was quite disappointing and left us with mixed feelings.

When we arrived, we were not greeted particularly warmly. But the biggest issue came when we started ordering.

We were told that our 3-year-old child had to pay €10 instead of €4, because apparently the prices are based on height. I asked if we could measure him properly, as he was 101 cm tall with his shoes on, and I even offered to take his shoes off, but nobody seemed willing to listen or discuss it.

For our second child, who is 12 years old, we were also charged the student price, even though we had documents confirming her age. She was around 152 cm tall with shoes on, and again, we were simply told that everything was based on height.

Personally, I find this pricing system very unfair and potentially discriminatory towards children based on their height. Children are growing very quickly nowadays, and a 10-year-old child can easily be 150–160 cm tall, but that does not mean they will eat or consume the same amount as an adult student. If a child is not actually a student, I don’t understand why they should automatically be charged the student price simply because of their height. Age should surely be taken into consideration, not just height.

Another issue was the drinks. Our child asked for one Sprite, but we were charged for unlimited drinks, even though we never requested that option.

The staff at the service counter also made the experience quite difficult. Some employees seemed to have difficulty understanding English, while others simply did not seem interested in listening to our questions or concerns.

For a 3-year-old, there was unfortunately very little suitable food. I managed to find some chips, which he didn’t eat, and in the end he only ate two small pieces of meat. A large part of the food was spicy, covered in sauces, or Asian-style dishes, which wasn’t suitable for a small child.

Overall, we were quite disappointed, especially considering that we travelled from Cork specifically for this place.

Parents with young children, please be careful and keep in mind that you may end up paying considerably more than you expect, especially if your children are close to the height limits. ❤️

I have been a regular visitor to Zucchini’s for almost 20 years. The food has always been excellent, and 99% of my restaurant and hotel reviews are positive. I am not someone who enjoys bashing businesses, which makes this review particularly disappointing.

I booked a table online for my wife, my parents in their 70s and our 10-month-old baby. The booking system offered the option to add an infant and asked about buggy and high-chair requirements. I completed the booking and received confirmation.

On arrival, I was told I had not booked for the infant and that there was no space for our group. I explained that I had booked correctly and tested the website on my phone, discovering that the infant appeared to disappear from the booking afterwards. I have screenshots and videos showing this.

When I calmly raised the issue, the owner became extremely confrontational, told me to leave and threatened to call the Garda. This was deeply upsetting for my family, particularly my 77-year-old father.

I want to give genuine credit to the assistant manager, who was polite, respectful and understanding. He acknowledged that there appeared to be an issue with the website and immediately tried to resolve the situation. Unfortunately, by that stage, we no longer felt comfortable remaining and decided to leave.

Why I have been forced to post this review

I initially posted a review on TripAdvisor and deliberately waited 24 hours to give the owner an opportunity to reflect and contact me. No such contact came.

The restaurant’s response to my TripAdvisor review is inaccurate and fails to tell the full story. It states that the issue was resolved, but completely omits the threats made to intimidate me and my family. It also fails to acknowledge that we were respectful throughout, and that the assistant manager treated us with courtesy and professionalism.

The owner was the person who was rude and confrontational, she was the only member of staff that we had any issue with. She did not have the manners to acknowledge any mistake, either at the restaurant or afterwards, and instead blamed me for a problem with the booking system.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that I can now see the option to add an infant has been removed from their website. The issue appears to have been corrected, yet there has still been no apology.

I have therefore felt forced to post this Google review as well as my TripAdvisor review, because I do not believe the restaurant’s response accurately reflects what happened.

I have huge sympathy for the staff here, particularly the assistant manager, who handled a very difficult situation with professionalism and respect.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience – make sure you get a written quote

I wish I had read the reviews before leaving my car at this garage, so I went there on Thursday, 10 September, expecting straightforward, professional service. Before going to this garage, I had actually been quoted €240 by Tony Brady Garage for the work. I therefore had a reasonable idea of what the job was likely to cost and was considering my options.

I needed my tyre pressure sensors replaced. I had already bought replacement sensors from a website my mechanic recommended. A gentleman who appeared to be the owner asked one of the lads to check them. After testing them, I was told that they could not be programmed and therefore could not be used.
I then asked if the garage could supply and fit their own sensors. I was told that the total cost would be €95 for all four tyres. Given that I had previously been quoted €240 elsewhere, I considered €95 to be a very reasonable price and agreed to have the work done.I left my car around 11 am and my contact details. I was told that the car would be ready by around 1 pm.

I spent approximately two hours walking around town waiting for the call. As my NCT appointment was around 3 pm, I was conscious of the time. When I still had not received a call, I decided to sit a few metres from the garage and wait. At approximately 2 pm, I went back in. The first thing that struck me was the facial expression of the lad who had worked on my car when I asked whether it was ready. He directed me to the office, where the owner was on the phone. One of his subordinates then handed me a bill for €380.

At first, I genuinely thought I had been given the wrong bill. Unfortunately, I was then told that the €95 I had understood to be the total cost was actually €95 per tyre. My problem was never that a garage should not charge for labour, parts or its expertise. My issue was that €380 was completely different from the price I understood we had agreed to before I left my car there.

Had I been clearly told the cost would be €380, I would have had the opportunity to make an informed decision — particularly as I had already been quoted €240 by another garage.

I explained that I could not afford the unexpected €380 bill. I was offered the option of paying the amount in instalments, but that was not the point. The issue was the unexpected price and the fact that it was not what I understood we had agreed.

When it became clear that I was not prepared to pay €380, the owner agreed to remove the sensors on the condition that I pay €50. At that point, I felt I had little choice but to accept because the garage still had my car keys and locknut.

What upset me most was not simply the money. It was the way I felt I was treated when I questioned the bill. When I tried to explain my concerns, I was met with comments such as “It’s all about you.” At one stage, I was asked to leave the office while I was still trying to explain my position and resolve what I believed was a genuine misunderstanding. Eventually, the owner left the office with my keys.

I left feeling extremely disappointed, frustrated and disrespected.
My advice to anyone using this garage is simple: get the full price in writing before handing over your keys and authorising any work. Make sure you know whether the quoted price is for the entire job or per tyre/per item. Do not rely solely on a verbal quotation.

I am sharing this review because I would not want someone else to find themselves in the same situation — particularly if they have somewhere important to be and suddenly discover that the price they understood to have been agreed has increased from €95 to €380.

For me, this was not about refusing to pay for work. It was about clarity, transparency, communication and how a customer is treated when there is a disagreement over the price.

I attended Truly Dental Tullamore for a consultation, in-person examination and scans for complex implant treatment. I received a personalised written plan dated 25 April which stated “IV Sedation included” and “10% discount for full, upfront payment.” I paid €1,000 that day and the remaining €13,415 on 14 May — €14,415 in total.

After the full payment had been accepted, I was told that general anaesthesia would cost a further €2,500, later reduced to €1,500. I repeatedly asked how this related to the IV sedation already stated as included and how the written 10% discount had been applied. I never received a clear, itemised answer.

I was later told that I had rescheduled surgery three times, including cancellations within 48 hours, that my €1,000 deposit would be retained and that another €14,415 was outstanding. This was wrong: the full amount had already been paid, and the dates I postponed were cancelled with more than 48 hours’ notice. For example, the 22 July appointment was cancelled 12 days beforehand because I had a medical procedure scheduled six days before it. After I supplied proof of payment, Truly withdrew that position and confirmed that nothing would be deducted, but never properly explained how such a serious error had occurred.

A promised revised treatment plan was never supplied. Clinical questions about the proposed sinus augmentation and anaesthesia were acknowledged but not answered before the replacement dates passed.

After months of back-and-forth and a formal complaint, Truly closed the treatment plan and refunded the €14,415 in full. I acknowledge that the refund was unconditional and complete, but I was left without treatment, without the promised answers and several months later no closer to getting my teeth fixed. Other providers I approached either could not offer an appointment until February 2027 or indicated substantially higher costs.

I was initially impressed by the clinic, which makes the outcome especially disappointing. Anyone considering paying a very large sum upfront for complex treatment should insist on a fully itemised written plan, exact anaesthesia costs, every promised discount and firm clinical answers before paying anything.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Truly Dental.

UPDATE FOLLOWING THE OWNER’S RESPONSE

I honestly find this response disingenuous. It gives the impression that I have not already tried to discuss the matter, when I spent months going back and forth with Truly Dental about recovering my money, the discount I was promised and the additional charges introduced after my payment had been accepted in full.

A generic invitation to contact you again does not address a single specific point raised in my review. I think the contrast between the detail in my review and this response speaks for itself.
